criticisms.target: The conclusion that on this evidence agreement is the one thing that should not raise your confidence
criticisms.criticism: To survive the counter-argument that algorithmic agreement mathematically indicates a higher probability of factual correctness the work must prove that unanimous LLM consensus yields a higher absolute error rate than a single model's isolated output.

criticisms.target: The claim that roughly three-quarters of the independence you appear to be buying is lost
criticisms.criticism: To survive the counter-argument that even highly correlated ensembles consistently reduce variance and improve baseline performance the work must demonstrate that this correlation actively degrades output quality rather than merely offering diminishing returns.

criticisms.target: The assertion in The honest half that gaining 10 to 23 points on near-tie decisions represents a problem because it is concentrated on unseen calls
criticisms.criticism: To survive the counter-argument that automatically resolving ambiguous edge cases is the exact primary value of secondary validation the work must show that a 10 to 23 point improvement on difficult calls is not worth the near-zero computational cost of the extra check.

criticisms.target: The claim that human disagreement is not noise it is the product
criticisms.criticism: To survive the counter-argument that human disagreement often reflects subjective bias or cognitive error the work must prove that human variance consistently produces more accurate ground-truth decisions than a correlated AI panel.

criticisms.target: The application of the formula n_eff to LLM reviewers
criticisms.criticism: To survive the counter-argument that deterministic algorithmic ensembles do not behave identically to human survey respondents the work must empirically validate that this sixty-year-old survey statistics formula accurately predicts the actual failure rates of modern AI panels.
